name: The Sun
story: The centre of the solar system — a G2V main-sequence star, 4.6 billion years old, fusing 600 million tonnes of hydrogen into helium every second. Holds 99.86% of the system's total mass; everything else is leftover dust. Surface temperature ~5,500°C; core ~15 million°C. The photosphere is what we see; the corona stretches millions of kilometres beyond it and reaches ~1 million°C — one of physics's open mysteries (why is the corona hotter than the surface?).
comparison: Light from the Sun takes 8 minutes 17 seconds to reach Earth — a snapshot of how the Sun was 8 minutes ago. The Sun is 333,000× more massive than Earth.
